definition: Incantation linguistics: the linguistic sources, lexical composition, and phonetic features of incantations, reflecting religious and cultural fusion
core_finding: The Golden Hoop Mantra 'Oṃ Maṇi Padme Hūṃ' is a Sanskrit transliteration; the Five Thunder Spell is a Han-Chinese Daoist term; Wukong's cursing 'impudent fiend' is Ming-dynasty colloquial speech — three linguistic sources reflecting Three-Teachings synthesis

linguistic_insights: Eight incantations reflect Three-Teachings synthesis: Sanskrit (Buddhist) + Daoist terminology (Daoist) + colloquial speech (folk)
The Golden Hoop Mantra is the only purely Sanskrit transliteration, reflecting the esoteric Buddhist mantra tradition
The Five Thunder Spell combines Daoist terminology with Classical Chinese officialese, reflecting Daoism's inheritance of Han-dynasty bureaucratic prose
Wukong's taunts are Ming-dynasty street speech, reflecting Sun Wukong's folk-hero image
The Tang Monk's admonition is Buddhist precept language in Classical Chinese, reflecting his monastic identity
The Buddha's sermon is in Xuanzang's translation style, the pinnacle of Buddhist scriptural Sinicization
The diversity of linguistic sources reflects the Three-Teachings synthesis of Journey to the West
